title: POC Invoke SDKs Toolchain Integration Playback
summary: Progress sync for POC integration focusing on SDK function-calling, structured output stability, and fallback behavior. Customer ran 48h soak; saw occasional schema drift and KV cache misses at higher concurrency. Discussed telemetry gaps, suggested SDK patch (v0.9.3) and a fallback playbook; agreed next steps: run 3 targeted end-to-end experiments, share security artifacts, and schedule a perf run under dedicated capacity next week.
next_steps: Tomás to provide patched SDK wheel and integration notes by 2026-04-24
Customer to run 3 end-to-end scenarios and upload logs to shared folder by 2026-04-28
Redwood and Crescendo to schedule dedicated-capacity perf run (2 hour window) week of 2026-04-27
Lena to share SOC2 + network configuration checklist and private deployment docs by 2026-04-25
Priya + Maya to align on acceptance criteria and sign-off plan by 2026-05-01
action_items: Owner: Tomás Rivera - Build and publish SDK patch v0.9.3 with improved function-calling schema validation - Due: 2026-04-24
Owner: Aisha Rahman - Run 3 nominated scenarios (low/high concurrency, long prompt, tool fallback) and upload zipped logs - Due: 2026-04-28
Owner: Evan Liu - Capture network trace during next perf window and share pcap + notes - Due: 2026-04-30
Owner: Lena Park - Send SOC2 summary + Private deployment network checklist - Due: 2026-04-25
Owner: Maya Chen - Draft acceptance criteria doc and propose sign-off flow - Due: 2026-05-01
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-23 11:00 PT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Tomás (SE), Samir, Maya; Aisha, Jared, Priya, Evan, Nora (Crescendo)

Auto-summary (auto): quick recap of last week, runs, and blockers

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this to an hour, quick roll call?
[00:10] Aisha: hi, Aisha here (Lead ML), Jared on for the CTO, Priya and Evan are here too, Nora is joined in a bit
[00:20] Tomás: tomas here, samir and maya from redwood on the call as well
[00:28] Lena: sweet, agenda — runbook updates, SDK patch, perf finding, security asks, decide next perf window

[02:00] Aisha: quick update from our side — we ran the 48 hour soak on the staging cluster, used the SDK baseline 0.9.1 and our retry layer, overall success rate was like 98.1% but we saw structured output failures on ~1.9% of calls, most were schema mismatches on the billing tool invocation, sometimes missing the transaction_id field
[02:30] Priya: yeah and the product team saw the downstream parser reject ~40 of those events, so it's non-trivial

[04:10] Tomás: ok that maps to what we suspected — a couple of edge cases where function-calling returns an array instead of object when the model hallucinate a collapsed response, and our SDK at 0.9.1 wasn't strictly enforcing the JSON schema on tool responses, we should be able to catch that with pre-parse validation
[04:42] Samir: also noticed that under ~45 rps the KV cache prefix hits were fine but at sustained 120 rps we saw a spike in misses which increased latency P95 by ~120 ms

[06:05] Evan: we captured some traces, from our side it looked like tcp retransmits around the time of the misses, not sure if it's network or the cache eviction behavior on the host
[06:30] Nora: from a privacy perspective we want to ensure any logs we upload are redacted; we can't share full PII tokens

[07:10] Lena: noted, we'll provide a redaction script; quick question — are you on hosted or dedicated staging for this soak?
[07:18] Aisha: hosted for the initial soak; requested dedicated for the perf run next week per your suggestion

[08:00] Tomás: proposed fix is two parts: SDK-side strict schema validation and a graceful fallback path where if the function payload doesn't match the expected schema we reroute to a lightweight verification model or return a structured error code that the app can use to invoke a secondary path
[08:25] Priya: how invasive is the SDK change? we don't want to have to rewrite our schemas for existing calls

[09:10] Tomás: minimal — the SDK will add an opt-in validation flag and surface a single validation hook; by default behavior stays the same for now, opt-in for strict mode; the patch will be v0.9.3
[09:40] Aisha: can you also log the raw model output in a safe way? we need to debug the hallucinated array->object change

[10:15] Samir: yes we can ship an optional debug flag that writes a sanitized delta to the log bundle, we will ensure the redaction script strips emails and tokens, etc

[11:00] Jared: cost question — in prior notes you mentioned a caching strategy that reduces token cost; if we enable fallback verification models won't that increase cost significantly?
[11:18] Tomás: good point — the fallback model would be a small, cheaper verifier (e.g., a 3B distilled model) and we only call it on validation failures, so overall token cost increase should be marginal; we can quantify in the perf run

[12:50] Priya: about the KV cache — is the miss pattern something we can tune with prefix caching or does it require deeper runtime changes?
[13:10] Samir: two levers — conservative prefix length and aggressive cache warming; for your workload the access pattern shows high prefix variance because prompts are slightly different per user, so we recommend enabling prefix compression + a warmup phase in the dedicated run; runtime kernel selection shouldn't be required yet

[14:45] Evan: we can try prefix compression, but I want to capture exact timings. propose we run a 2-hour dedicated capacity window and measure P50/P95/P99, token cost, and misses with tracing enabled

[15:10] Lena: agreed — we can provision a small dedicated pool for the window; Samir will own the run on Redwood side and Evan + Aisha will run the customer scenarios

[16:00] Aisha: one more issue — function-calling sometimes returns an extraneous meta field named "resp_hint" that our parser tries to upcast; is that a Redwood model artifact?
[16:20] Tomás: it's probably due to the model variant we used (we routed to rwd-lite-1) — sometimes training artifacts add helper hints, we can pin to a stricter variant or strip unknown keys in the SDK

[17:05] Priya: can we get the model catalog entry for rwd-lite-1 and a recommended pinned variant for production?
[17:20] Lena: yes, I'll attach the model catalog link in the recap — note that the catalog names might be slightly different in the transcript (auto transcription often mangles 'rwd' to 'readwood'), we'll include canonical names

[19:00] Nora: security ask — need KMS integration details and the data-retention policy for logs during the POC
[19:18] Lena: send it — we'll add the KMS integration doc and the retention defaults (30 days for debug logs, configurable for enterprise)

[20:45] Tomás: regarding telemetry gap — Aisha mentioned we currently don't capture function argument hashes in spans; adding that will help match parser rejections to raw model output
[21:00] Aisha: correct, without those we can't quickly triage when the schema mismatch happens

[22:30] Samir: we can add a small telemetry patch that includes an argument hash and a truncated model output (sanitized) in the span; it increases span size slightly but improves signal for debugging

[24:00] Priya: acceptance criteria check — what do we need to see to call the POC successful?
[24:15] Maya: good question — from Redwood's side we recommend: <1% structured output failures on the nominated scenarios, P95 latency within 350ms for common flows, and documented fallback behavior + logs for triage

[25:00] Priya: Crescendo team would like: no unhandled parser failures for the billing flow (0 allowed), and clear sign-off that fallback paths never expose PII

[26:00] Lena: we can adapt acceptance to be conservative for billing, zero tolerance, and provide a test harness so you can run synthetic cases to prove it

[27:20] Evan: for the dedicated perf run, do we need to change any network rules or ports? we run in a locked VPC with strict egress
[27:40] Samir: we'll provide a short checklist — basically allow outbound to the Redwood inference endpoints on 443, and if you want to keep control plane private we can talk private deploy options, but for the perf run hosted dedicated pool should be fine if you allow the endpoints

[29:10] Aisha: okay checklist works; about the logs we will only upload redacted bundles to the shared S3; can Redwood provide the redaction script?
[29:25] Lena: yes, Tomás will attach a python redactor and Samir will add instructions to run it before upload

[31:00] Tomás: quick demo — I pushed a branch showing the SDK validation hook, live run: calling billing.process(), you can see in the debug run when a tool returns an array we catch and reject before the app-level parser chokes
[31:25] (screen share noise)
[31:40] Aisha: hmm ok I see the log, it flagged an invalid payload with code INV_SCHEMA_01, that's useful

[33:00] Priya: could that error be surfaced in a more structured way to the product team? our pipeline expects a specific error contract
[33:15] Tomás: yes we'll map INV_SCHEMA_01 to a structured error with fields {code, hint, safe_preview} — again, opt-in for now

[34:50] Jared: going back to cost — do you have a ballpark delta for enabling debug flags and fallback verifier calls?
[35:05] Samir: rough estimate: debug logging adds ~2-5% overhead on token storage and a verifier call on failure rates could add cost proportional to failure rate; if failures are 2% and verifier is 1/10th cost of main gen, added cost ~0.2% overall; we'll put numbers behind it in the perf run

[36:50] Lena: let's lock the perf window — proposed slots: Tue 2026-04-28 14:00-16:00 UTC or Wed 2026-04-29 09:00-11:00 PT, which works?
[37:10] Evan: Tue 14:00 UTC works for us
[37:20] Aisha: that's fine

[38:00] Maya: I'll block it and create the test matrix — scenarios include low concurrency happy path, high-concurrency churn, long prompt chain with tool hops, and forced schema failure paths

[39:20] Priya: how will we measure structured failures? what log fields should we capture?
[39:40] Samir: capture: request id, invoke timestamp, raw model output (sanitized), validation result code, downstream parser result; include span arg hash to correlate

[40:30] Lena: i'll follow up with a short recap email with links: model catalog, SDK patch PR, perf run calendar, SOC2 + KMS docs, and the redaction script

[41:10] Aisha: quick nit — in the earlier runs we saw a small memory spike in the SDK host process when debug mode is enabled, can you confirm memory will be safe at scale?
[41:30] Tomás: we observed a ~30 MB bump in our staging test at 200 rps with debug frames on; it's linear with the number of concurrent spans; we'll add an upper-bound guard to avoid OOMs

[43:00] Jared: any legal/procurement blockers we should preview?
[43:15] Lena: standard enterprise SOW + NDA already in place, we'll prepare a short SOW for the dedicated perf engagement and include data handling terms

[44:10] Nora: about the retention you mentioned 30 days for debug logs — can that be shortened to 14 for our environment?
[44:25] Lena: yes retention is configurable, for Private deployments you can set retention to 0; for hosted POC we can set it to 14 days as a compromise

[45:30] Tomás: going to summarize tech changes we will deliver: SDK v0.9.3 with opt-in strict validation, telemetry patch with arg hash, redaction script, and a troubleshooting checklist for the perf run

[46:10] Aisha: perfect. also can you include the exact error codes and mapping doc so our parser team can handle them cleanly?
[46:24] Tomás: yes will add an errors.md in the SDK repo

[47:00] Maya: one more ops question — for the perf run if we hit the P95 target but see high variance across tenants, how will we attribute?
[47:20] Samir: we will run tenant-isolated scenarios as part of the matrix; we can also correlate latency to prefix hit ratios and show per-tenant histograms

[48:45] Priya: do you prefer we open an internal cadence ticket for acceptance or will Redwood own sign-off docs?
[49:00] Lena: let's co-own — we'll draft acceptance criteria and you can annotate; once mutual sign off we move to a pilot SLA proposal

[50:20] Evan: any additional spikes we should watch for during the perf window?
[50:35] Samir: watch for cache evictions, model variant routing mismatches, and network jitter; we'll provide alerts hooks for the window

[52:10] Aisha: ok, thank you, this was productive, we have clear next steps

[52:30] Lena: quick recap aloud — Tomás SDK patch by tomorrow, run by Aisha by 28th, dedicated perf run Tue 28th 14:00 UTC, Lena will send docs, Maya will own acceptance doc, Maya will schedule a 30 min follow-up for initial perf readout on Wed 29th; anything else?

[53:10] Priya: please include the shared artifacts link in the recap, we'll only upload after redaction

[53:30] Lena: will do — artifacts: https://redwood.app/poc/crescendo/0423 (internal link), SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1122, perf matrix doc: /shared/poc/crescendo/perf-matrix-0423.xlsx

[54:20] Jared: one last thought — if we see persistent failures we may ask for a short canary on a private deploy but that's down the road

[55:00] Lena: noted; thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the CRM records

[56:10] (wrap up and sign-offs)
[57:00] Meeting end
